unverified: the Claim's last mile — "a run's squash-merge keeps the plan's title" — is not settled by this diff, and cannot be. M1–M4 pin the *fold commit's* subject; the squash-merge subject is GitHub's, and it equals the branch's single commit subject only when the pushed `ultra/integration-run-<N>` branch has exactly one commit. Two ordinary shapes break that link in code this patch does not touch: (i) a multi-wave run leaves one fold commit per wave on the branch, so GitHub's squash default falls back to the PR title rather than any commit subject; (ii) the post-fold reconcile path in `fleet/run-engine.mjs:1447` commits `wave <N> reconcile (attempt <K>)` on top of the candidate, so the branch head after that wave is the reconcile subject, not the plan title — M2 says "the integration branch's head after wave 1 has subject <title>", which holds only on the clean-adoption path the exam exercises. The RUNBOOK sentence M4 mandates ("A squash-merge takes the plan's title as its subject") therefore reads as unconditional while the mechanism is conditional. Nothing inside this task's FILES can settle it, and the exams the Proof names are all green, so this blocks nothing. What would settle it: an end-to-end check that the pushed branch is single-commit (or that the PR title is itself the plan's H1) before the RUNBOOK states the squash-merge consequence flatly — plan-level work for the task that owns the PR-open path in `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`.

fleet/run-engine.mjs — in `sweepCacheDirs`, a failed removal is swallowed silently (`try { fs.rmSync(...); removed++ } catch { /* leave it */ }`), so the `driver:integrated-clean` event's `removed` count silently understates the sweep and nothing records that a cache directory survived. The consequence is bounded (a surviving `__pycache__` will surface as a red integrated `Run:`), but the diagnosis then points at the task rather than at the sweep. Suggest emitting a log line (the engine's `log(...)` is in scope at the call site) or carrying a `failed` count on the event so a permission/ENOTEMPTY failure is legible in the run record. The `readdirSync` catch is fine as-is: an unreadable directory is genuinely nothing to sweep.
